items.title: 3 U.S. Dividend Stocks Investors Are Watching As Rate Cut Hopes Fade
items.summary: Rising rate expectations are back in focus after fresh Fed commentary, and that shifts the spotlight onto large U.S. dividend payers trading on value metrics. When borrowing costs climb and policy feels less friendly, investors often pay closer attention to cash returns and sensible valuations. This piece walks through three stocks from our U.S. Large-Cap Value and Dividend screener that appear particularly exposed to this latest rate hike debate. items.title: PACCAR (PCAR) Stock Still Looks Undervalued After Its 113% Run
items.summary: PACCAR has delivered a 112.6% share price gain over the past 5 years, so the obvious question now is whether that move still lines up with the cash the business is expected to generate. With the stock recently closing at US$105.57, investors are increasingly asking if the current tag is supported by the trucking group's underlying cash flows or if expectations have run ahead of the fundamentals. items.title: What’s Going On With PACCAR (PCAR)?
items.summary: PACCAR (PCAR) has been pulled into focus after its shares lagged the wider market over the past year, as softer trucking conditions and elevated fuel costs weighed on fleet spending and new vehicle demand. Recent trading has been choppy for PACCAR, with the share price down about 19% over the past 90 days and 5% year to date. items.title: 3 Boring Dividend Stocks With Customers That Keep Coming Back
items.summary: Uniforms, pool chemicals and truck parts rarely make headlines, yet three companies paying dividends this week kept raising payouts through recessions and housing busts. Each has a catch, and one stock has lost more than half its value in five years.
